genZNote: Partially acid-fast — enough to make you think Mycobacterium, not enough to actually be one.

morphology.shape: Branching, filamentous rod resembling fungal hyphae
morphology.arrangement: Branching filaments that can fragment into rod/coccoid forms
morphology.size: Filaments of variable length, ~0.5-1.2 µm wide
morphology.notes: Weakly/partially acid-fast on modified (weak) acid-fast stain — a key distinguishing feature from Actinomyces, which is not acid-fast at all

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil and decaying organic matter worldwide
habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental saprophyte; opportunistic pathogen, especially in immunocompromised hosts

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive, branching, beaded filaments; partially acid-fast

culture.colonyMorphology: Dry, chalky, folded colonies, often with a musty "wet cardboard" odor
culture.pigmentation: Variable — white, tan, orange, or yellow depending on species

identificationClues: Branching, filamentous Gram-positive rods resembling fungal hyphae on Gram stain
Weakly/partially acid-fast on modified acid-fast stain — distinguishes it from the morphologically similar but acid-fast-negative Actinomyces
Slow-growing, dry, chalky colonies with a characteristic musty odor
Risk factor profile skews toward immunocompromised hosts (unlike Actinomyces, more linked to mucosal disruption)

diseases: CNS nocardiosis (brain abscess) — often via hematogenous spread from a pulmonary focus
clinicalImportance.transmission: Inhalation of organisms from contaminated soil/dust; direct inoculation into skin (e.g. thorn injury) for cutaneous disease
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: An opportunistic pathogen particularly affecting immunocompromised patients (e.g. those on chronic corticosteroids, transplant recipients, or with HIV/AIDS)
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Partial acid-fastness is the key laboratory feature separating Nocardia from Actinomyces, which otherwise looks very similar on Gram stain and shares a similar filamentous/branching morphology

examFacts.importantDisease: Pulmonary and CNS nocardiosis in immunocompromised hosts
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Partially acid-fast, unlike the morphologically similar Actinomyces, which is not acid-fast at all
